headline: Histology anchors 3D reconstruction and gene-panel prediction in spatial transcriptomics
label: Histology Anchored Spatial Transcriptomics Reconstruction
summary: New methods use H&E morphology to reconstruct continuous 3D expression, predict 1,000-gene panels and statistically dissect histology–expression links.
synthesis: The dominant thread treats histology as the scaffold for recovering spatial expression beyond what is directly measured. HIM-INR uses a histology-informed multi-task implicit neural representation to infer continuous 3D gene expression from sparse sections. THiRST builds multi-resolution 3D volumes from serial 2D sections through morphology-guided registration. GeneFlow applies flow matching with histology and gene tokenizers to predict panels of up to 1,000 genes from H&E. MorphoANOVA adds an inferential layer, using nested spatially varying coefficient models and sequential ANOVA to test gene-wise morphology–expression dependence. CroSP integrates expression, location and histology through cross-view contrastive graph autoencoding. A second strand sharpens resolution: st2sc infers single-cell profiles from multicellular spots, and SpaAxFormer imputes gene-resolved states across spatial neighbors with axial transformers. GeneSPOT uses optimal transport to track spatial gene-relationship reorganization across conditions and time. Multimodal embedding models such as scHiR and Bloom are adjacent but are not spatial.
